ctd_blind_local_v3 — round 1

Build a model of this CTD phosphorylation time course that explains the measured distributions, and say what it implies about how P-TEFb modifies the substrate. Report explicitly what these data can and cannot establish about the mechanism. In particular, test whether the modification of a repeat changes the rate at which its immediate neighbours in the array are modified, against the alternatives that the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified (cooperativity between repeats) or on nothing at all, and say which of these the data can and cannot separate. Also test the earlier conclusion, drawn by eye, that the kinase acts distributively rather than processively.

winner: product_load_inhibition (decisive)

question
Build a model of this CTD phosphorylation time course that explains the measured distributions, and say what it implies about how P-TEFb modifies the substrate. Report explicitly what these data can and cannot establish about the mechanism. In particular, test whether the modification of a repeat changes the rate at which its immediate neighbours in the array are modified, against the alternatives that the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified (cooperativity between repeats) or on nothing at all, and say which of these the data can and cannot separate. Also test the earlier conclusion, drawn by eye, that the kinase acts distributively rather than processively.
system
RNA polymerase II CTD (8 heptarepeats, in vitro), phosphorylated by P-TEFb (CDK9/cyclin T1); mass-spectrometry time course
inference target
mechanism_discrimination
success criteria

R_PI_onPTEFb → PTEFb_Imodifiers: CTD_1, CTD_2, CTD_3, CTD_4, CTD_5, CTD_6, CTD_7, CTD_8vial * kon_I * PTEFb * (CTD_1 + 2 * CTD_2 + 3 * CTD_3 + 4 * CTD_4 + 5 * CTD_5 + 6 * CTD_6 + 7 * CTD_7 + 8 * CTD_8)
R_PI_offPTEFb_I → PTEFbvial * koff_I * PTEFb_I

Parameters

idvalue / assignmentstatus
kmod= 0.01ESTIMATED in [1e-05, 1]
cp= 1ESTIMATED in [0.2, 5]
q_proc= 0fixed
K_ATP= 50fixed
nb= 1ESTIMATED in [0.01, 100]
kon_I= 0.001ESTIMATED in [1e-07, 0.1]
koff_I= 1fixed
Antimony source of the winner (model/antimony)
model ctd_ptefb_counts
  // CTD_n: CTD molecules with n of 8 repeats phosphorylated (one bit per repeat)
  compartment vial = 1;
  species CTD_0 in vial, CTD_1 in vial, CTD_2 in vial, CTD_3 in vial, CTD_4 in vial;
  species CTD_5 in vial, CTD_6 in vial, CTD_7 in vial, CTD_8 in vial;
  species ATP in vial, ADP in vial, PTEFb in vial;
  CTD_0 = 100; CTD_1 = 0; CTD_2 = 0; CTD_3 = 0; CTD_4 = 0;
  CTD_5 = 0; CTD_6 = 0; CTD_7 = 0; CTD_8 = 0;
  ATP = 3000; ADP = 0; PTEFb = 1;
  kmod = 0.01; cp = 1.0; q_proc = 0; K_ATP = 50;
  // single-repeat encounters: one modification per binding event (distributive)
  J0: CTD_0 + ATP -> CTD_1 + ADP; 0;
  J1: CTD_1 + ATP -> CTD_2 + ADP; 0;
  J2: CTD_2 + ATP -> CTD_3 + ADP; 0;
  J3: CTD_3 + ATP -> CTD_4 + ADP; 0;
  J4: CTD_4 + ATP -> CTD_5 + ADP; 0;
  J5: CTD_5 + ATP -> CTD_6 + ADP; 0;
  J6: CTD_6 + ATP -> CTD_7 + ADP; 0;
  J7: CTD_7 + ATP -> CTD_8 + ADP; 0;
  // processive encounters: j repeats per binding event, continuation probability q_proc (0 in base)
  Jp0_2: CTD_0 + 2 ATP -> CTD_2 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_3: CTD_0 + 3 ATP -> CTD_3 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_4: CTD_0 + 4 ATP -> CTD_4 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_5: CTD_0 + 5 ATP -> CTD_5 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_6: CTD_0 + 6 ATP -> CTD_6 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_7: CTD_0 + 7 ATP -> CTD_7 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_8: CTD_0 + 8 ATP -> CTD_8 + 8 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^7*CTD_0;

all 7 flags, in full
  • design_summary role guess is WRONG and is corrected here: phos1_rel..phos8_rel are measurement columns (relative MS intensities for 1..8 phosphates), not design factors; their 'levels' are measured values, and the 2916-cell 'factorial' is meaningless. The file has NO condition columns: one in vitro condition (8-repeat CTD 100 uM, P-TEFb catalytic, ATP 3 mM) sampled at 4 times. All 9 phosN_rel columns are mapped as separate observables of that single condition; condition_columns is empty and the label template is a fixed string.
  • ctd_ms_timecourse.csv, all columns phos0_rel..phos8_rel, all 4 rows: intensities are on a per-injection arbitrary scale that differs between time points (row sums 1.00 at 0 min, 4.07 at 60 min, 3.79 at 120 min, 0.85 at 960 min, matching the lab note) while total substrate is conserved. Values are NOT commensurable across time points as they stand. No processing was declared: the note does not say the data were normalised, and the note's own observation model (a per-time-point factor mapping amounts onto intensities, which also scales the noise SD) belongs model-side. Do not pool or compare raw values across rows.
  • ctd_ms_timecourse.csv: 19 of 36 measured values are exactly 0.0 (row time_min=0: phos1_rel..phos8_rel; row 60: phos7_rel, phos8_rel; row 120: phos8_rel; row 960: phos0_rel..phos7_rel). The note states additive Gaussian noise of a single SD at every peak, under which a measured empty peak would scatter around zero (including small negatives), not sit at exactly 0.0. These exact zeros look like not-detected or absent peaks written as zero, or idealised values, but the source states no detection floor and no handling rule, so no below_detection entry is declared. Left as is and NOT excluded; the observation model should know that roughly half the likelihood terms are exact zeros of uncertain provenance.
  • No replicates (n = 1 per species per time point, stated in the note) and no error column. error_type recorded as 'none' because the file carries no error estimate. The note describes the noise model (additive, normal, one SD for the whole experiment shared by all peaks, scaled per time point by the same factor that maps amounts onto intensities); that SD is not given and must be estimated by the observation model. This is not an SD/SEM call: no error bars exist.
  • Information content is thin for mechanism discrimination. Of 4 time points, t = 0 carries only the initial condition (all substrate unmodified; phos0_rel = 0.99957). t = 960 min carries only completion (only phos8_rel nonzero). Effectively only the 60 and 120 min distributions carry shape information about rates, each losing one degree of freedom to its own scale factor. The readout is phosphate COUNT only (9 mass peaks); which repeats are modified is not observed, so position-dependent (neighbour) effects can only enter through their imprint on count distributions.
  • time_min = 960 is a sampled time (16 h), not a declared steady-state measurement, and is mapped as 960, not inf. It appears to be at or near completion (all signal in phos8_rel), but treating it as steady state would be a modelling decision, not an extraction edit.
  • Time units are minutes, consistent with the intent's horizon (960 min). No conversion was made.

      "rationale": "The readout is intact-mass MS of the 8-heptarepeat CTD construct (the lab note names it). Species are in uM with vial = 1, so no volume factor is needed. If a position-resolved candidate is fitted, this label maps to its single zero-mark configuration. Units are relative intensities on a per-injection scale (data_labels: arbitrary). The lab note shows spectra summing to 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 at 0, 60, 120 and 960 min while substrate is conserved. A scale factor is therefore required, indexed per time point and shared by all nine peaks under group ctd_ms, because one injection gives one spectrum and one gain. No offset: no background, blank or instrument floor is described, and the exact zeros in the table argue against an unsubtracted baseline. The absolute scale is pinned by the fixed model total: CTD_0 starts at 100 uM, the total over CTD_0..CTD_8 is conserved, and that amount must stay unestimated. Pinning the first factor to 1 would instead clash with the t=0 spectrum summing to 1 against 100 uM. The factors are thus intensity per uM, roughly 0.010, 0.041, 0.038 and 0.0085, consistent with the nominal-magnitude gap. Noise: the lab note states additive normal error, one SD for the whole experiment, equal for every peak, scaling between time points with the same factor that maps amounts onto intensities. That is the gain-scaled shape sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms, with one sigma_ctd_ms shared by name across all nine observables. Per-peak sigmas would rest on 4 points each and collapse toward zero on peaks the model fits exactly. data_signals is inconclusive (n = 1, no replicates), so this choice follows the lab note rather than a replicate test. The scale stays lin because this peak is zero once (log illegal) and the error is stated to be additive. An assumption that cannot be tested here: every phosphorylation count has the same ionisation and detection response. A count-dependent response factor would be confounded with the cooperativity parameter cp, so it is named rather than estimated.         "CTD_4": 0.0,
        "CTD_5": 0.0,

        "ADP": 0.0,

      "preequilibration": false,
      "rationale": "The intent lists no perturbation. The data hold a single label: one purified in vitro P-TEFb kinase reaction, sampled at 0, 60, 120 and 960 min with no replicates. That makes exactly one condition, and none is invented. The overrides only restate the reaction mix as the lab note gives it (tier direct: the note states amounts and sampling times), so the audit can see what this condition was. These values match the model's initial values, so they change nothing in the simulation. CTD_0 = 100 uM, the recombinant 8-heptarepeat substrate, all unmodified at the start of the reaction. CTD_1..CTD_8 = 0 uM, since no modified substrate exists at t = 0. ATP = 3000 uM (3 mM at start, model unit uM, so there is no unit slip). ADP = 0 uM, as no phosphoryl transfer has occurred yet. PTEFb = 1 relative unit: the glossary says it is catalytic and constant, with its absolute concentration absorbed into kmod; the note gives no kinase concentration, so 1 is a convention, not a measured dose. No assignment rules or initial assignments exist, so these initial-value overrides are not silently ignored. The CTD_0 = 100 uM total is what pins the absolute scale in the observation draft. Its per-time-point gains (intensity per uM) are identified only because this total is fixed and unestimated. Estimating it would make it degenerate with the scale factors. Likewise, kmod absorbs kinase amount, so PTEFb must stay fixed. No parameter is overridden. kmod, cp and q_proc are mechanism parameters to be estimated or switched by model selection, not properties of this condition. The glossary marks none of them 'set per condition', which is expected for a single-condition design. K_ATP stays at its construction-fixed 50 uM. No population factor exists, so nothing is split per group. Pre-equilibration is false. t = 0 is the moment kinase, substrate and ATP are combined, not a settled baseline. basal_state confirms that the model's only steady state is full modification (CTD_8), so pre-equilibrating would run the reaction to completion before the first sample. Correction to design_summary: phos1_rel..phos8_rel were guessed as 'design' factors, but they are measurements (relative MS intensities for 1..8 phosphates), like phos0_rel. Their few unique values reflect only four rows with exact zeros, not factor levels. The 2916-cell 'factorial' is therefore spurious."
    }
  ]

Each one's declared neutral value was simulated against the base model and reproduced it to a relative 1e-06, so these candidates are EXACTLY nested: same generated code, same integrator, and a ΔAIC between them is a statement about the parameter table.

A SPECTRUM, not a rank. A direction many decades below the largest is a parameter combination the data barely constrain; a spectrum with no such direction proves nothing, because this is a local screen at one point. A model can be comprehensively non-identifiable and still predict well — the flat combinations and the prediction bands are two halves of one sentence, and neither blocks unless the intent says parameter values are the deliverable.

Structural flat directions, before the fit and at it

structural flat directions: none before the fit, none at it

A structural direction is flat at every parameter value, so it is flat near the nominal and around the optimum alike; one flat in only one of the two places is local, not structural. An indicator: AIC and BIC charge every estimated parameter. Method: the residual Jacobian at the MLE (the information screen's own) and at 2 random points within ±0.5 (scaled units) of it, each normalised, stacked; each pre-fit direction is tested along its own vector (the candidate's `structural_nulls_at_mle` record).

9Epistemics

What the data cannot distinguish7

MUTENeighbour-dependent rates (nb) versus a count-dependent rate profile with more than one shape parameter. …
MUTEProcessive versus distributive modification on the selected structure. …
MUTEPositive count cooperativity versus processivity (and versus molecule-to-molecule rate heterogeneity, not in the model …
MUTEThe identity of the global slowdown. Inhibition of P-TEFb by ADP and by phosphorylated CTD both equal Σn·CTD_n by …
MUTEkon_I and koff_I separately. koff_I is fixed at 1.0, so only K_I = koff_I/kon_I ≈ 1.1 mM is estimated. …
MUTEK_ATP and any ATP-depletion effect. K_ATP is fixed at 50 µM, and ATP stays at or above about 2.2 mM throughout, so the …
every entry, in full
  • Neighbour-dependent rates (nb) versus a count-dependent rate profile with more than one shape parameter. Counts-only MS sees the configuration-averaged rate per count. Diagnosis

SELECTED MECHANISM. product_load_inhibition is the round-0 winner M5_neighbour_and_count plus one global term, and it has the following parts. (a) It is distributive by construction: q_proc is fixed at 0.0. …

full diagnosis

SELECTED MECHANISM. product_load_inhibition is the round-0 winner M5_neighbour_and_count plus one global term, and it has the following parts. (a) It is distributive by construction: q_proc is fixed at 0.0. (b) The per-repeat rate is modulated by a neighbour factor nb = 0.311 and a count factor cp = 1.627. (c) ATP is saturating: K_ATP is fixed at 50 µM, while ATP never falls below about 2.2 mM (3 mM minus at most 0.8 mM consumed). (d) Free P-TEFb is inhibited by the accumulated phosphate load Σn·CTD_n, which equals the ADP produced. K_I = koff_I/kon_I = 1.0/0.000909 ≈ 1.1 mM, with koff_I fixed. If the rate tracks free P-TEFb, that is about 27% slowing at the ≈410 µM load reached by 2 h and about 42% at the 800 µM end point. Scores: AIC −172.80 and Akaike weight 0.961. The base is at ΔAIC 6.40 with weight 0.039. The indistinguishable set is {product_load_inhibition}. Only 2 of the 4 models in the declared lattice were visited, and the unvisited corners are untried, not rejected. There is no held-out series, so the selection rests on AIC alone. WHY IT WINS (attribution). ΔnLLH is 4.20, worth 8.40 likelihood units against 2 parameter units. Of that, 2.44 is earned in the 60- and 120-min spectra, as a net of gains and losses spread over nine peaks. Gains: phos5@60 +2.02 (winner 0.293, base 0.250, measured 0.352), phos2@120 +1.09, phos6@60 +0.87, phos4@60 +0.80, phos2@60 +0.64. Losses: phos1@60 −1.43, phos8@120 −1.21, phos6@120 −0.83, phos7@120 −0.64. The other 1.76 units come from the t0 and t960 points. Both models fit those to within 0.1σ, except phos7@960, which costs the winner 0.34. They pay only because the shared sigma fell from 1.012 to 0.890 µM. Switching kon_I off without refitting costs 188.8 AIC units. Refitted (that is, the base), it costs 6.4, because kmod drops from 0.00514 to 0.00458 to compensate. So the term mainly reshapes the progress curve rather than adding a large independent effect. The mean number of marks per molecule is 2.48 at 1 h and 4.13 at 2 h. First-order depletion of repeats at a constant ≈0.0062 min⁻¹ already predicts 4.19 at 2 h, so the overall deceleration does not by itself demand a global brake. OBSERVATION MODEL. Each peak's intensity is sc_t × the amount in µM, with a linear transformation. The scales are sc_ctd_ms_t0 = 0.00999, sc_ctd_ms_t60 = 0.0404, sc_ctd_ms_t120 = 0.0393 and sc_ctd_ms_t960 = 0.0086 per µM. For 100 µM of conserved substrate these give totals of 1.00, 4.04, 3.93 and 0.86, against measured 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85. Noise is additive normal with one sigma_ctd_ms = 0.890 µM for all peaks, scaled by the same sc_t. In intensity units that is σ = 0.0089, 0.036, 0.035 and 0.0077 at the four time points. FIT QUALITY. Sigma is fitted and there are no replicates, so χ² = 36 = n_data by construction and no absolute goodness-of-fit test exists. About 35 of the 36 χ² units sit in the 18 points at 60 and 120 min, because each t0 and t960 spectrum is fitted trivially by its own scale factor. The fitted σ is therefore about √2 smaller than the scatter of the informative points. That inflates every σ-unit below and sharpens the likelihood behind ΔAIC. On the 60/120-min points alone the margin would be roughly 2×2.44−2 ≈ 2.9 AIC units, weight about 0.8: still above the 2.0 threshold, so the selection stands, but less sharply than 0.961 suggests. WHAT IS STILL WRONG. All residuals are single unreplicated points, so the case rests on sign agreement across the two informative spectra. - High counts: at both 60 and 120 min the winner puts mass at 7 and 8 marks that the data lack. Residuals: phos7@60 −0.66σ, phos8@60 −0.10σ, phos7@120 −2.35σ, phos8@120 −2.78σ (the last two are the largest in the fit). - Middle counts: it puts too little at 5–6 marks: phos5@60 +1.65σ, phos6@60 +1.64σ, phos6@120 +2.05σ. - Late time: it leaves about 0.9% of molecules at 7 marks at 16 h (phos7@960 −0.97σ), and the data have none. - The zero at phos8@120 is not a detection floor. Measured 8-mark CTD is 0 at 2 h while 7-mark CTD is 0.19, and a 0-mark peak of 0.061 was detected in the same spectrum. - So the data want the last one or two modifications specifically slowed early, yet complete by 16 h. The global product-load term brakes every step instead: it raised phos8@120 from 0.088 to 0.097. - A weaker, isolated residual at 60 min: phos1 +2.18σ, with phos0 −1.57σ and phos3 −1.48σ. MECHANISM ANSWERS. Round-0 log-likelihoods are given. AICs below assume each variant adds one parameter to a 6-parameter independent model, consistent with the 8-parameter M5. ΔAIC to the winner: M5 6.4, neighbour-only M3 18.3, count-only M2 23.5, processive-only M4 24.9, independent M1 62.1. 1. 'Rate depends on nothing' is rejected (−log L −61.36 vs −95.40). The measured distributions are broader than binomial: the variance of marks per molecule is 2.57 against 1.71 at 1 h, and 2.63 against 2.00 at 2 h. 2. Neighbour-only beats count-only by about 5.2 AIC, and both together beat neighbour-only by about 11.9. Dropping cp costs 6.95 nllh units and dropping nb 9.56. nb and cp move by less than 3% between the two round-1 candidates. 3. But intact-mass MS sees only the configuration-averaged rate at each count. A neighbour effect projects onto an effective count-dependent rate profile, and M5's need for two shape parameters is what a two-parameter or free per-count count-only profile could also supply. That model was not fitted, so 'neighbour over count' holds only against the one-parameter count form. 4. Distributive vs processive was not tested on the selected structure, because q_proc is fixed at 0.0 in both round-1 candidates. The only processive model fitted, M4 (processive with otherwise independent rates), loses to M5 by about 18.5 AIC, but it changes two things at once. Against count-only M2 it differs by only about 1.4 AIC, below the 2.0 threshold. Processivity and positive count cooperativity both broaden count distributions, and the data do not separate them as single additions. The distributions are unimodal at 60 and 120 min, with no unmodified-plus-heavily-modified bimodality. That is consistent with the by-eye distributive reading but does not exclude a partial processive component. 5. The cause of the global slowdown is not identifiable. ADP and phospho-CTD both equal Σn·CTD_n by stoichiometry, and in a single condition progress is monotone in time, so time-dependent kinase inactivation is confounded with both. IDENTIFIABILITY. The local FIM is full rank with a 3.72-decade eigenvalue spread (threshold 8) and no flat directions. The smallest eigenvector is dominated by kon_I (0.993, with kmod at 0.111). Profiles were not computed, so no parameter interval is known. kon_I is the least-determined parameter: its K_I lies above the maximal load of 0.8 mM, so only the initial slope of inhibition is seen. RECOMMENDATION. Revise, with one move: free q_proc on product_load_inhibition. This is the test of the distributive conclusion that the intent asks for and that the winner currently assumes. The next move after that is a count-only model with a high-occupancy slowdown term, fitted against nb. It targets the 7–8-mark misfit and tests whether the neighbour term is separable from count dependence at all.

Misfit hypotheses

  • 1 (best supported, unaddressed by any visited model). A slowdown specific to the last one or two modifications is missing: the per-repeat rate falls once a …
  • 2. The product-load term partly stands in for distribution shape rather than reporting an independent inhibitory process. …
  • 3. A partial processive component, or molecule-to-molecule rate heterogeneity (not in the model space), contributes to the broader-than-binomial distributions …
all 4 hypotheses, in full
  • 1 (best supported, unaddressed by any visited model). A slowdown specific to the last one or two modifications is missing: the per-repeat rate falls once a molecule carries about 6 or more marks, or terminal/sequence-divergent repeats are poor substrates. Evidence: n=7,8 are over-predicted at both informative times (phos7@120 −2.35σ, phos8@120 −2.78σ, phos7@60 −0.66σ) and n=5–6 under-predicted (phos5@60 +1.65σ, phos6@60 +1.64σ, phos6@120 +2.05σ). Measured 8-mark CTD is 0 at 2 h while a 0.061 peak was detected in the same spectrum, and conversion is complete by 16 h. The global product-load term does not supply this: it worsened phos8@120 (0.088 → 0.097) and created phos7@960 −0.97σ. Count-dependent and position-dependent versions cannot be separated from intact-mass counts; middle-down or positional MS, or single-repeat mutants, would separate them.
  • 2. The product-load term partly stands in for distribution shape rather than reporting an independent inhibitory process. Evidence: the mean marks per molecule (2.48 at 1 h, 4.13 at 2 h) matches constant-rate first-order site depletion (≈0.0062 min⁻¹ predicts 4.19 at 2 h). Switching kon_I off unrefitted costs 188.8 AIC units, but refitted it costs only 6.4, with kmod compensating from 0.00514 to 0.00458. Of the 4.20 nllh gain, only 2.44 is earned at 60/120 min, spread as wins and losses over nine peaks. ADP inhibition, phospho-CTD inhibition and time-dependent kinase inactivation would all appear this way in one condition. An ADP spike-in, a second ATP/ADP ratio, or late enzyme addition would separate them.
  • 3. A partial processive component, or molecule-to-molecule rate heterogeneity (not in the model space), contributes to the broader-than-binomial distributions now carried by cp alone. Evidence: variance of marks 2.57 vs 1.71 binomial at 1 h and 2.63 vs 2.00 at 2 h. Processive-only and count-only additions to the independent model differ by only ≈1.4 AIC (−log L −80.95 vs −81.64). Untested on the selected structure because q_proc is fixed at 0.0; freeing it there is the separating move.
  • 4 (lowest as a cause of mechanism misfit). Observation layer: absent peaks are recorded as exact zeros (phos7@60, phos8@60, phos8@120 and every absent peak at t0/t960), which additive Gaussian noise cannot produce. The 18 trivially fitted t0/t960 points also shrink the shared sigma by about √2 relative to the informative scatter, inflating every σ-unit (phos8@120 would be ≈−2.0σ) and the likelihood margin. The noise model is the study team's stated decision and is not changed here. The phos8@120 zero is not a detection-floor artefact, because a smaller peak (phos0@120 = 0.061) was detected in the same spectrum.

It sums all 70 four-mark configurations, which the assay cannot tell apart; this is the glossary's CTD_4 lump (uM, vial = 1). A position-resolved candidate sums its 70 configurations here. Signals are relative per injection (units arbitrary; spectrum sums of 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 over conserved substrate). So there is one scale factor per time point, shared across the nine peaks of each spectrum (group ctd_ms), and no offset because no background is described. The absolute scale is pinned by the fixed, unestimated 100 uM CTD total. Noise is additive normal with one experiment-wide SD equal for every peak, scaled by that spectrum's gain, per the lab note: sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms with a single shared sigma_ctd_ms. With no replicates, data_signals is inconclusive and the lab note decides. The scale is lin because there are 2 zeros (log illegal) and the error is additive. Equal MS response across counts is assumed rather than estimated, because a count-dependent response would be confounded with cp. Evidence: direct (lab note).
- **observable** `obs_phos5` = `CTD_5` (lin): This is the intact-mass MS peak for five phosphates (lab note). It sums the 56 isobaric five-mark configurations, which is the glossary's CTD_5 lump (uM, vial = 1). A position-resolved candidate sums those 56 here. Intensities are arbitrary and drift between injections (spectrum sums of 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 while substrate is conserved). That calls for one gain per time point shared by all nine peaks of the spectrum (group ctd_ms), with no offset because no background or blank is stated. The absolute scale is pinned by the fixed, unestimated 100 uM total. Noise is additive normal, with one SD for all peaks and the whole experiment, scaled by each spectrum's gain, as the lab note states: sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms with one shared sigma_ctd_ms. data_signals is inconclusive (no replicates). The scale is lin because there are 2 zeros (log illegal) and the error is additive. Equal ionisation across counts is assumed and stated; it is not estimated because it would trade off against cp. Evidence: direct (lab note).
- **observable** `obs_phos6` = `CTD_6` (lin): This is the intact-mass MS peak for six phosphates (lab note). It sums the 28 isobaric six-mark configurations, which is the glossary's CTD_6 lump (uM, vial = 1). A position-resolved candidate sums those 28 here. Signals are relative per injection (units arbitrary; spectrum sums of 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 over conserved substrate). So there is one scale factor per time point, shared across the spectrum's nine peaks (group ctd_ms), and no offset because no background is described. The absolute scale is fixed by the unestimated 100 uM total rather than by pinning a factor. Noise follows the lab note: additive normal error, one experiment-wide SD equal for every peak, scaled per time point by the same gain, giving sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms with a shared sigma_ctd_ms. data_signals is inconclusive (n = 1). The scale is lin because there are 2 zeros (log illegal) and the error is additive. Equal response across counts is assumed rather than estimated, since it is confounded with cp. Evidence: direct (lab note).
- **observable** `obs_phos7` = `CTD_7` (lin): This is the intact-mass MS peak for seven phosphates (lab note). It sums the 8 isobaric seven-mark configurations, which is the glossary's CTD_7 lump (uM, vial = 1). A position-resolved candidate sums those 8 here. Intensities are arbitrary per injection (spectrum sums of 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 over conserved substrate), so there is one gain per time point shared by all nine peaks (group ctd_ms). No offset, as no background is reported. The absolute scale is pinned by the fixed, unestimated 100 uM total. This peak is zero at 3 of 4 times, which rules out a log scale and any pure proportional noise. The lab note's additive normal error, one SD for every peak scaled by each spectrum's gain, fits that: sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms with one shared sigma_ctd_ms. A sigma for this peak alone would collapse to zero on its three exact zeros, which is why the sigma must be shared. data_signals is inconclusive (no replicates), so the lab note decides. Equal MS response across counts is assumed rather than estimated, because it would trade off against cp. Evidence: direct (lab note).
- **observable** `obs_phos8` = `CTD_8` (lin): This is the intact-mass MS peak for the fully modified construct (lab note). Because Ser2 and Ser5 are mutually exclusive, 8 phosphates means every repeat is marked: the single configuration that is the glossary's CTD_8 (uM, vial = 1). A position-resolved candidate maps this label to its all-marked configuration. Signals are relative per injection (units arbitrary; spectrum sums of 1.00, 4.07, 3.79 and 0.85 over conserved substrate). So there is one scale factor per time point, shared by the nine peaks of the spectrum (group ctd_ms), and no offset because no background or blank is described. The absolute scale is pinned by the fixed, unestimated 100 uM CTD total, not by pin_first_to_one. The peak is zero at 3 of 4 times, so log and pure proportional noise are illegal. The lab note states additive normal error with one experiment-wide SD for every peak, scaled by each spectrum's gain: sc_ctd_ms * sigma_ctd_ms with one shared sigma_ctd_ms. A sigma for this peak alone would be unidentifiable from one nonzero point. data_signals is inconclusive (n = 1). Equal ionisation across counts is assumed rather than estimated, since it is degenerate with cp. Evidence: direct (lab note).

- **condition** `cond_invitro_PTEFb_CTD8` <- 'invitro_PTEFb_CTD8', overrides {'CTD_0': 100.0, 'CTD_1': 0.0, 'CTD_2': 0.0, 'CTD_3': 0.0, 'CTD_4': 0.0, 'CTD_5': 0.0, 'CTD_6': 0.0, 'CTD_7': 0.0, 'CTD_8': 0.0, 'ATP': 3000.0, 'ADP': 0.0, 'PTEFb': 1.0}: The intent lists no perturbation. The data hold a single label: one purified in vitro P-TEFb kinase reaction, sampled at 0, 60, 120 and 960 min with no replicates. That makes exactly one condition, and none is invented. The overrides only restate the reaction mix as the lab note gives it (tier direct: the note states amounts and sampling times), so the audit can see what this condition was. These values match the model's initial values, so they change nothing in the simulation. CTD_0 = 100 uM, the recombinant 8-heptarepeat substrate, all unmodified at the start of the reaction. CTD_1..CTD_8 = 0 uM, since no modified substrate exists at t = 0. ATP = 3000 uM (3 mM at start, model unit uM, so there is no unit slip). ADP = 0 uM, as no phosphoryl transfer has occurred yet. PTEFb = 1 relative unit: the glossary says it is catalytic and constant, with its absolute concentration absorbed into kmod; the note gives no kinase concentration, so 1 is a convention, not a measured dose. No assignment rules or initial assignments exist, so these initial-value overrides are not silently ignored. The CTD_0 = 100 uM total is what pins the absolute scale in the observation draft. Its per-time-point gains (intensity per uM) are identified only because this total is fixed and unestimated. Estimating it would make it degenerate with the scale factors. Likewise, kmod absorbs kinase amount, so PTEFb must stay fixed. No parameter is overridden. kmod, cp and q_proc are mechanism parameters to be estimated or switched by model selection, not properties of this condition. The glossary marks none of them 'set per condition', which is expected for a single-condition design. K_ATP stays at its construction-fixed 50 uM. No population factor exists, so nothing is split per group. Pre-equilibration is false. t = 0 is the moment kinase, substrate and ATP are combined, not a settled baseline. basal_state confirms that the model's only steady state is full modification (CTD_8), so pre-equilibrating would run the reaction to completion before the first sample. Correction to design_summary: phos1_rel..phos8_rel were guessed as 'design' factors, but they are measurements (relative MS intensities for 1..8 phosphates), like phos0_rel. Their few unique values reflect only four rows with exact zeros, not factor levels. The 2916-cell 'factorial' is therefore spurious.
